title: "Elite Pocket Passer Who Can Run": Skip Bayless Celebrates Vanderbilt's Massive Jared Curtis Flip - NewsBreak
text:
By Manhaz Muntaha ,
39 minutes ago Five-star quarterback Jared Curtis flipped his commitment from the Georgia Bulldogs to the Vanderbilt Commodores . He had been committed to Georgia since May,
Skip Bayless Celebrates Vanderbilt’s Massive Jared Curtis Flip (Image Via Instagram/@jcurtis.2) The move positions Clark Lea and the Commodores to stay competitive after current star quarterback Diego Pavia departs. Pavia is a leading Heisman candidate and has already said that this will be his final college season.
Pavia actively recruited Curtis, which potentially opened the door for Curtis to start next season as a true freshman. Outspoken analyst Skip Bayless is one of many to be excited for Curtis’ move to Vandy.
“My school Vanderbilt just flipped 5-star QB recruit Jared Curtis from signing w GEORGIA. He can step right in for what should be Heisman winner Diego Pavia, start next 3 years, be 1st QB drafted after winning a Chip. He’s 6-4, 225 – elite pocket passer who can run. #AnchorDown,” Bayless tweeted.
Curtis plays for Nashville High School in Tennessee, which is located roughly 10 miles from Vanderbilt’s campus. He is set to sign with the Commodores on Wednesday morning.
Curtis is the No. 1 quarterback nationally in the 2026 class, and he is now Vanderbilt’s highest-rated recruit in program history. He has thrown for 9,528 yards, 123 touchdowns and 25 interceptions in four seasons of his high school career.
Jared Curtis Explains Why He Flipped From Georgia to Vanderbilt Curtis’ decision to switch his commitment to Vanderbilt on Tuesday came with plenty of twists. After several Rivals analysts reported that he had already told Georgia’s staff he planned to sign with the Commodores, Curtis jumped tweeted to deny those claims.
Not long after, Curtis posted another message addressing the situation in full and revealing why he ultimately stepped away from his Georgia pledge.
“I do love Georgia, I love the coaches and players there,” Curtis wrote. “They have been so good to me and my family. I know they would do everything to help me be successful. They have been the best program in the country for a reason. The past year it’s where I wanted to be and definitely where my parents have wanted me to go.
“That’s part of what makes this so hard. You try to make everyone who has been good to you and done so much for you happy, and when you can’t it sucks. But I gotta walk my path that feels right in my heart, at the end of the day this has to be my decision.”
Curtis initially committed to Georgia in early 2024, decommitted late in the year, recommitted this May. He has now parted ways with the Bulldogs again.
